Title: Meet Copilot Chat: where to find it

Title: Write better prompts: goal, context, source, expectations
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: The 4-part recipe for a great prompt
WhyItMatters: A little extra detail in your request gets you a much better first answer and less back-and-forth.
TipSteps: Start with your goal (what you want) | Add context (who it's for and why) | Say what it should look like (bullets, table, tone, length) | Name any source to use, then refine with a follow-up
TryPrompt: Write a short, friendly reminder to my team that timesheets are due Friday. It's for busy staff who skim email, so keep it under 80 words with one clear call to action.
LearnLabel: Get started writing prompts in Microsoft Copilot
Notes: Learn page 200 OK (last updated Feb 2026); explicitly describes the four parts goal/context/expectations/source and says only a clear goal is required. Companion pages: 'Write a great prompt in Microsoft Copilot' and 'Get better Copilot responses with great prompting' (both 200). Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft 365 Copilot help & learning', published Feb 27 2026; description covers goal, context, expectations and iterating.

Title: Summarize a long email thread in Outlook
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Catch up on any email thread in seconds
WhyItMatters: Get the key points of a long back-and-forth without scrolling through every reply.
TipSteps: In Outlook, open the long email conversation | Select Summary by Copilot (or Summarize) at the top of the thread | Read the summary and click the numbered citations to jump to the original emails
TryPrompt: Summarize this email thread in 3 bullets: what was decided, what's still open, and what I need to do next.
LearnLabel: Summarize an email thread with Copilot in Outlook
VideoLabel: Summarize and draft emails with Microsoft 365 Copilot in Outlook
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; steps taken from page (button reads 'Summary by Copilot' or 'Summarize'; on iOS/Android tap the Copilot icon). Page embeds a short video. Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft Learn', published Jul 29 2025. Licensing: Microsoft's 'What Copilot license do I have' and 'How Copilot Chat works in Microsoft 365 apps' pages say all subscribers have access to Copilot in Outlook; unlicensed users get standard (not priority) access. Not supported on encrypted/IRM emails or shared mailboxes. TryPrompt is for the Copilot chat pane in Outlook if they want more than the button gives.

Title: Draft an email with Copilot in Outlook
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Beat the blank email
WhyItMatters: Copilot writes a solid first draft from a one-line request, so you just review, tweak and send.
TipSteps: In Outlook, start a New mail (or a reply) | Select the Copilot icon in the toolbar, then Draft (classic Outlook: Draft with Copilot) | Type what you want to say and select Generate | Adjust length or tone, select Keep it, then edit and send
TryPrompt: Write a polite email declining a meeting invitation for next Tuesday, offering two alternative times later in the week.
LearnLabel: Draft an email message with Copilot in Outlook
VideoLabel: 5 Ways to Use Copilot in Outlook | Microsoft 365
Notes: Learn page 200 OK (old /office/...3eb1d053 URL redirects here); steps match page for new Outlook/web and classic. UI labels vary: new Outlook 'Draft' + 'Keep it'; classic 'Draft with Copilot' + 'Keep'; Mac 'Insert'. Draft doesn't work on plain-text messages in new Outlook (switch to HTML). Newer builds also show 'Help me write'/'Help me reply'. Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft Copilot', published Jun 10 2026 (covers drafting new emails, replies, and revising tone/length). Licensing: Copilot in Outlook is included for all subscribers per Microsoft's license pages.

Title: Check Copilot's work (and keep it safe)
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Trust, but verify
WhyItMatters: Copilot is a great helper but can make mistakes, so a quick check keeps your work accurate and your data protected.
TipSteps: Look for the small citation numbers in the answer, or select Sources at the bottom | Open a source and double-check names, numbers and dates before you share | Only use content you're allowed to share and follow company rules for sensitive info (e.g. never paste passwords) | Select thumbs down to flag a wrong answer
TryPrompt: Before I use this, list any facts, figures or dates in your last answer that I should double-check, and tell me where each one came from.
LearnLabel: What information does Copilot use to answer my prompt?
VideoLabel: How grounding works in Microsoft 365 Copilot
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; covers grounding, citations, 'review the sources and confirm critical details', Copilot respects existing permissions and doesn't train public models on company data. Citation/Sources steps from 'Control and review sources of Microsoft Copilot Chat's responses' (support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/control-review-sources-copilot-chat, 200). For the privacy angle, Microsoft Learn 'Enterprise data protection in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat' (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/enterprise-data-protection, 200). 'Never paste passwords' is our friendly house rule, not a Microsoft quote - align with your own policy. Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft 365 Copilot help & learning', published Mar 12 2026.

Title: Upload a file and ask Copilot about it
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Hand Copilot a file and ask away
WhyItMatters: Get a quick summary or answers from a long PDF, Word doc or spreadsheet without reading every page.
TipSteps: In Copilot Chat, type what you want, e.g. Summarize the document | Select the + (Add content) button, then Upload images and files or Attach cloud files | Pick your file and select Send | Tip: you can also type / and start typing a file name to add it
TryPrompt: Summarize this document in 5 bullet points, then list any deadlines, dollar amounts or action items it mentions.
LearnLabel: Analyze an uploaded document in Copilot Chat
VideoLabel: Analyze an uploaded document with Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; states Copilot Chat is included with work subscriptions; page embeds a video. '/' file referencing from 'Refer to specific files and more in Microsoft Copilot' (200) - its 'Users without a Microsoft Copilot license' section confirms unlicensed users can reference files with '/' (people/emails/meetings need a license). Button name varies by page/version: 'Add content and agents', 'Add and manage sources' or '+'. File upload is 'standard access' for unlicensed users (may be limited at peak times). Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft 365 Copilot help & learning', published Apr 18 2025.

Title: Get email coaching before you hit send
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: A second opinion on that tricky email
WhyItMatters: Copilot suggests how to improve tone and clarity so important emails land the way you intend.
TipSteps: Write your email in Outlook as usual | Select the Copilot icon in the toolbar and choose Coaching by Copilot | Review the tone, clarity and reader sentiment suggestions | Apply the ones you like (or Apply all suggestions), then send
LearnLabel: Get email coaching with Copilot in Outlook
Notes: Learn page 200 OK (old /office/...91a3cd56 URL redirects here); steps match page for Windows, Mac and mobile. Page embeds its own short video. On mobile the draft must be at least 100 characters. No dedicated official YouTube video on coaching found, so left blank. Licensing: Copilot in Outlook is included for all subscribers per Microsoft's license pages; if Coaching isn't visible, check with IT.

Title: Catch up on a busy Teams chat
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Missed 200 chat messages? No problem
WhyItMatters: Get the main points, decisions and action items from a long chat without scrolling back through everything.
TipSteps: In Teams, go to Chat and open the conversation | Select Open Copilot in the upper-right corner | Pick a suggested prompt or type your own | Select Sources to jump to the original messages
TryPrompt: Summarize what I've missed in this chat over the last week, including any decisions and anything assigned to me.
LearnLabel: How to use Microsoft Copilot in Teams chats and channels
VideoLabel: AI Simplified | Catch up on chat threads with Copilot in Microsoft Teams
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; steps match. Default look-back is 30 days; Copilot can't summarize images, Loop components or shared files in the chat. Channels also have a 'Summarize thread' option (thread needs 1000+ characters). Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft Teams'. Unlicensed users can still use Copilot Chat in Teams (Chat > Copilot) for general questions, but in-chat summaries need the license.

Title: Recap a Teams meeting (or ask during one)
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Never lose track of a meeting again
WhyItMatters: Get key points and action items from a meeting you missed, or quickly catch up if you join late.
TipSteps: After the meeting, open it from your Teams Calendar or the meeting chat and go to the Recap tab | Select Open Copilot and ask a question | During a live meeting, select Copilot in the meeting controls to ask privately | Make sure transcription is on so you can ask about it afterward
TryPrompt: What were the main decisions and action items from this meeting, and who owns each one?
LearnLabel: Catch up on meetings with Microsoft Copilot in Teams
VideoLabel: Catch up your way with Copilot in Teams
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; covers during-meeting use (Copilot in meeting controls, 'View prompts', late-joiner catch-up) and after-meeting use (meeting chat 'Open Copilot' and Recap tab). Asking questions after the meeting requires a transcript. Copilot won't work in meetings hosted outside your organization. Organizer controls this via Meeting options > Copilot and other AI. Page embeds a short video. Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft Teams', published Jun 25 2026 (covers Meeting Recap, audio/video recaps).

Title: Summarize a long Word document
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Get the gist of any document fast
WhyItMatters: Know what a long report, contract or policy says before you dive into the details.
TipSteps: Open the document in Word (saved in OneDrive or SharePoint works best) | If a summary appears at the top, select View More | Or open Copilot and type: Summarize this document | Use the citations to check key points in the original
TryPrompt: Summarize this document in 5 bullet points for someone with 2 minutes, then list any open questions or action items.
LearnLabel: Create a summary of your document with Copilot in Word
VideoLabel: How to Summarize Documents in Word
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; auto-summary at top needs a Copilot license and a file saved in OneDrive/SharePoint (200+ words). 'Summarize this document' prompt from 'Chat with Copilot about your Word document' (support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/copilot/chat-with-copilot-about-your-word-document, 200, embeds a video). Since Apr 15 2026 Copilot inside Word/Excel/PowerPoint/OneNote is for licensed users (label 'M365 Copilot (Basic/Premium)'); unlicensed staff can upload the file to Copilot Chat instead (see upload tip). Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft Copilot', published May 1 2026.

Title: Draft a first version in Word
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Let Copilot write the first draft
WhyItMatters: Go from a blank page to a workable draft in minutes, then add your own expertise.
TipSteps: Open a blank document (or place your cursor where you want new text) | Open Copilot in the bottom-right corner and describe what you need: topic, audience, tone, length | Type / to point Copilot at a file if you have one, then select Generate | Keep, regenerate or refine it - or select any text and ask Copilot to rewrite it
TryPrompt: Draft a one-page overview of our new visitor check-in process for front-desk staff. Use a friendly tone, short paragraphs, and a numbered list of steps.
LearnLabel: Draft and add content with Copilot in Word
VideoLabel: Compose and summarize documents with Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; steps match 'Create a draft with Copilot' section (Copilot opens bottom-right; '/' to reference a file; Generate; keep/discard/regenerate/refine). Page also covers rewriting selected text; see also 'Edit content and rewrite' (support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/copilot/edit-rewrite-content, 200) with Replace/Insert below/Regenerate. Some experiences are rolling out gradually. Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft Learn', published Jul 29 2025 (older UI may differ slightly).

Title: Summarize a PowerPoint deck
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: 40 slides? Get the highlights
WhyItMatters: Understand the key points of a long presentation before a meeting without clicking through every slide.
TipSteps: Open the presentation in PowerPoint | Select the Copilot button to open the Copilot pane | Type Summarize this presentation and send | Try Show key slides or Show action items next
TryPrompt: Summarize this presentation in 5 bullets, then list 3 questions the audience is likely to ask.
LearnLabel: Summarize your presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; steps match; summarizes up to ~40,000 words; page embeds a video. The Copilot button location varies (ribbon on this page; newer PowerPoint pages say bottom-right of the slide). Title: Ask Excel questions about your data
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Ask your spreadsheet a question
WhyItMatters: Spot trends, totals and outliers in plain English, no formulas required.
TipSteps: Open a workbook with your data | Select the Copilot icon in the lower-right corner of Excel | Ask a question and name the columns you care about | Review the result (and ask Copilot to explain any formula it adds)
TryPrompt: Which region had the highest and lowest sales? Show the answer as a chart and explain any outliers.
LearnLabel: Get data insights with Copilot in Excel
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; prompt ideas and 'name the columns' tip from page; also supports 'Explain the formula in the selected cell' - great for inherited workbooks. Copilot in Excel opens in edit mode by default and can change the workbook; choose Chat only mode to just ask questions ('Get started with Copilot in Excel', 200). Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft Copilot', published Jun 17 2026 (uses workout data as the example).

Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: From messy notes to clear summary
WhyItMatters: Turn pages of meeting or call notes into a tidy summary or to-do list you can share.

TryPrompt: Summarize the notes on this page in bullet points, then create a to-do list with any tasks and due dates mentioned.
LearnLabel: Summarize your OneNote notes with Microsoft Copilot
Notes: Learn page 200 OK (old /office/...89e1f3cd URL redirects here); steps match (Home tab > Copilot, compose box, Send, Copy). WhyItMatters: Ask quick questions, draft replies or pick up a desktop chat while you're away from your desk.

LearnLabel: Get started with the Microsoft Copilot mobile app

Title: Save your favorite prompts to reuse
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Stop retyping your best prompts
WhyItMatters: Save prompts you use often so you can rerun them with one click instead of retyping.
TipSteps: Run a prompt you like in Copilot Chat | Hover over your prompt and select the bookmark icon (Save prompt), then give it a clear name | Later, select a prompt pill or ... below the message box to open the Prompt Lab | Go to Your saved prompts and pick one
TryPrompt: Review and summarize today's emails and provide a list of action items.
LearnLabel: Save your favorite prompts to use again
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; steps combine this page with 'Changes to the Copilot Prompt Lab' (support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/changes-to-the-copilot-prompt-gallery-app, 200), which says the standalone app was retired July 2025 and prompts now live in the Prompt Lab inside Copilot Chat. Video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft 365 Copilot help & learning'; its description says the gallery is in Copilot Chat included with business subscriptions. TryPrompt is Microsoft's own example; the email part needs a license, so unlicensed users should save a web/file prompt instead.

Title: Tell Copilot how you like your answers
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Teach Copilot your preferences
WhyItMatters: Set your preferences once (like bullets, plain English or short answers) and Copilot uses them every time.
TipSteps: In Copilot Chat, select ... Settings and more, then Chat settings | Select Personalization and find Custom instructions | Select Edit instructions and describe how you like responses | Select Save instructions
TryPrompt: Use plain, jargon-free English. Start with a one-line summary, then use short bullet points. Keep answers under 150 words unless I ask for more.
LearnLabel: Customize how Microsoft Copilot responds to you
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; steps match. Microsoft Learn 'Manage Copilot personalization and memory' (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/copilot-personalization-memory, 200) states Copilot memory is available to Copilot Chat users with and without a license; admins can turn personalization off. Related: 'Manage Copilot Memory' (say 'remember that...', manage/delete in Chat settings) and temporary chat. No official Microsoft YouTube video found (only third-party), so left blank.

Title: Turn a Copilot answer into a shareable Page
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Keep and share Copilot's best answers
WhyItMatters: Save a useful answer as a Page you and your team can edit and keep building on, instead of losing it in chat history.
TipSteps: Ask Copilot Chat for something you'll reuse, like a checklist or plan | Below the response, select ... then Edit in Pages (or the pencil button) | Edit the page yourself or ask Copilot to update it | Share it with colleagues; find it later in your Library
TryPrompt: Create a one-page checklist for onboarding a new team member in their first week, with sections for Day 1, Days 2-3 and Days 4-5.
LearnLabel: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Pages
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; states Pages is available to work accounts with SharePoint/OneDrive storage, including without a Copilot license. Steps match ('Edit in Pages', pencil button, Library). Page embeds its own video. YouTube video verified via oEmbed; channel 'Microsoft Copilot', published Sep 16 2024 - an early look, so buttons may look different. Related: Copilot Notebooks ('Get started with Microsoft Copilot Notebooks', 200) collects files, chats and pages in one place, also available to Copilot Chat users.

Title: Let Prompt Coach improve your prompts
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Get a personal prompt-writing coach
WhyItMatters: Prompt Coach looks at your request and suggests a clearer version, so you learn to get better answers.
TipSteps: Open Microsoft Copilot (microsoft365.com) and select Agents in the left panel | If Prompt Coach isn't listed, select All agents and add it | Paste a rough prompt and ask Prompt Coach to improve it | Use the improved prompt in Copilot Chat
TryPrompt: Here's my prompt: 'write something about our holiday schedule.' Ask me any questions you need, then rewrite it into a clear prompt using goal, context, source and expectations.
LearnLabel: Agents built by Microsoft
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; lists Prompt Coach among Microsoft-built agents you add from 'All agents'. Microsoft Learn 'Agents for Microsoft Copilot Chat' (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/agents, 200) says agents grounded in instructions/public websites (like Prompt Coach) are available at no extra cost in Copilot Chat. Caveat: your admin must allow the agent - if it's missing or shows an error, contact IT. Also see Learn 'Create a Prompt Coach agent from a template' (200). Only third-party YouTube videos found, so left blank.

Title: Use Researcher for deeper research
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Your personal research assistant
WhyItMatters: Researcher digs through the web and your work files to produce a structured, source-cited report on complex questions.
TipSteps: In the Microsoft Copilot app, select Researcher under Agents | Type a specific question and say where to look (web, work files or both) | Answer its follow-up questions or say Go ahead | Review the report and its citations before you share it
TryPrompt: Research the key trends affecting our industry over the next 12 months. Use both web sources and my work files, and give me a one-page report with a summary, 5 key trends and cited sources.
LearnLabel: Get started with Researcher in Microsoft Copilot
Notes: Learn page 200 OK; steps match (Agents > Researcher; clarifying questions; 'Go ahead'; structured cited report). Researcher needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and takes several minutes.
